name: Editbay 2.1
body:
Editbay 2.1: a security fix for projects from other people, one Mac download for every Mac, captions that animate, tracks that reorder by dragging, and a faster timeline, export and start.

### Which file do I need?

- **Windows 11:** `Editbay-2.1-Windows-Setup.exe`
- **Any Mac**, Apple Silicon or Intel: `Editbay-2.1-Mac.dmg`. It runs on Apple Silicon from macOS 14 Sonoma and on Intel from macOS 13.4 Ventura.

The two "Source code" files are only for building Editbay yourself.

### Security

- **Update before exporting a project someone else sent you.** A project file from someone else could make its export write files outside the export folder and reach another computer. Every earlier version has this. 2.1 refuses such a file as damaged when it opens.
- A project file holding numbers no recording has could freeze Editbay as it opened. It is now refused as damaged.
- Editbay is built on Electron 44.10.2, with the security fixes of the six Electron and Chromium releases since the version 2.0 shipped with.

### Added

- **Captions animate** in and out with Fade, Pop, Slide up or Slide down, a whole line at a time or word by word as each is said. The export draws the same frames as the preview.
- **Tracks move by dragging** their header up or down, with their clips, and the Captions track moves among the video tracks the same way. The order shows in the preview and the export.
- Clicking a track's header shows that track in the Inspector.

### Changed

- **One Mac download for every Mac**, in place of one for Apple Silicon and one for Intel. Follow face uses ONNX Runtime 1.23.2 on both chips, the last with an Intel library.
- The Windows download is `Editbay-2.1-Windows-Setup.exe`, and the installer is 135 MB rather than 169 MB.
- Faster on long cuts: Select all then Group no longer freezes the window, and the timeline draws only the clips near the view.
- Faster exports: a picture in picture with rounded corners, an edge or a shadow two to six times, and many short pieces about a third faster on a computer with eight or more threads.
- Making captions for a long cut in many pieces gets its sound ready in under a second.

### Fixed

- The window opens at once, even when recordings sit on a computer that is switched off.
- On a Mac whose sound goes to a headset that is also a microphone, Editbay no longer asks for the microphone as it opens. macOS may ask once, at the first click.
- Dragging a piece of a group moves the whole group rather than breaking it.
- The preview's picture stays in step with the sound across cuts and after jump cuts.
- A crop number typed straight after choosing a picture is kept, and a text changed while another project opens stays in its own project.

The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ZazaGdev/editbay/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

### Windows

The installer is not code signed, so Windows SmartScreen warns about it: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

**SHA-256 of `Editbay-2.1-Windows-Setup.exe`:**
`180d9f36b0406778458373f9810eeb41d057587b9baf37f5bb8b5d28c15879ea`

Check it with `certutil -hashfile Editbay-2.1-Windows-Setup.exe SHA256`.

### Mac

1. Open the `.dmg` and drag Editbay into Applications.
2. Double-click Editbay. macOS says it could not verify it, because the app is not signed with an Apple certificate: click **Done**.
3. Open **System Settings**, **Privacy & Security**, scroll down, and click **Open Anyway** next to Editbay (it shows for about an hour after step 2). Enter your Mac's password, then **Open**. From then on Editbay opens normally.

Or in Terminal: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Editbay.app`.

**SHA-256 of `Editbay-2.1-Mac.dmg`:**
`a5431c80d946e898d28d6930ec7425bcdadc2c86bdc3af9f2acc6c8e9ce408dd`

Check it with `shasum -a 256 Editbay-2.1-Mac.dmg`.

Every download contains FFmpeg and FFprobe, which are under GPL-3.0. See [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](https://github.com/ZazaGdev/editbay/blob/main/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md), which carries the written offer for their complete source.

name: Editbay 2.0
body:
Editbay 2.0: Editbay on a Mac, clip speed, a Portrait picture in picture, a tidier Inspector, and a long list of fixes to the timeline, the preview and the export.

**Projects saved by 2.0 open only in 2.0 and later.** Editbay 1.0 to 1.2 say such a file needs a newer app. 2.0 opens every project the older versions saved.

### Added

- **Mac versions**, one for Apple Silicon and one for Intel, built and tested on GitHub's Macs. They are not signed by Apple; the README's **Mac** section says how to open them.
- **Clip speed**, in the Inspector, the preview and the export: a time-lapse up to 16x and slow motion down to 0.1x. The sound stays from 0.5x to 2x, keeping its pitch.
- **Portrait**, a tall 9 by 16 card like a phone, as a picture in picture shape beside Square, Rounded and Circle. It exports as previewed.
- **Remove background from the command search.** The pointer becomes a picker and the clip clicked next is the one it acts on. Make captions for a clip and Show where a clip came from work the same way.
- A sound clip can play one side of its track on both sides, for a voice recorded on the left only.
- A layer can have a look of its own, over its clip's.
- The command line's edit lists can lay layers, pictures, sound effects and music, end on a dip to black, and more. See `docs/edit-list.md`.

### Changed

- The Inspector's sections sit on cards, and Zoom is split into Framing, One-click zooms and Face.
- The sections right of the timeline fold down to a thin bar.
- The font lists offer the 30 fonts Editbay brings and the common ones on the computer.
- The preview's sound is seamless across cuts.
- Short notices show at the top in the middle, not over the Inspector.

### Fixed

- Speed changes, Ctrl+drag, gap closing and Remove silences keep sound in step with the picture where shots have J-cuts, L-cuts or separately recorded voice.
- A locked track refuses every edit to its clips, not only moves.
- A dip to black is darkest on the cut, and the blur transition blurs both ways.
- A recording that names BT.709 colours but no matrix keeps its colours in the export.
- Ctrl+wheel zoom, crop box resizing, export progress and the Export dialog's first draw behave as expected.
- Long, grouped timelines stay smooth during playback and edits.
- A project built by the command line shows a large OBS recording's picture on first open.

The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ZazaGdev/editbay/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

**SHA-256 of `Editbay.Setup.2.0.exe`:**
`0590862ac82193cc69700e556ff1d8fc6d0af853b37300109a70599ad9b94003`

The installer is not code signed. Check the hash with `certutil -hashfile "Editbay.Setup.2.0.exe" SHA256`.

**Mac:** `Editbay-2.0-arm64.dmg` for Macs with an M chip (macOS 14 Sonoma or later) and `Editbay-2.0-intel.dmg` for Intel Macs (macOS 13.4 Ventura or later).

1. Open the `.dmg` and drag Editbay into Applications.
2. Double-click Editbay. macOS says it could not verify it, because the app is not signed with an Apple certificate: click **Done**.
3. Open **System Settings**, **Privacy & Security**, scroll down, and click **Open Anyway** next to Editbay (it shows for about an hour after step 2). Enter your Mac's password, then **Open**. From then on Editbay opens normally.

Or in Terminal: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Editbay.app`.

**SHA-256 of `Editbay-2.0-arm64.dmg`:**
`13dc6dfa55b9ef073d8bb5dea0db5a788e580d1e010c070bc70578696b709536`

**SHA-256 of `Editbay-2.0-intel.dmg`:**
`7b071bd259c43586ee51ed62f2a9527fe5f9bee16239f6c0b1a0fa1a3fa43575`

Check a download with `shasum -a 256 Editbay-2.0-arm64.dmg`.

Every download contains FFmpeg and FFprobe, which are under GPL-3.0. See [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](https://github.com/ZazaGdev/editbay/blob/main/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md), which carries the written offer for their complete source.

name: Editbay 1.2
body:
Editbay 1.2: cropping that only crops, and fixes to J-cuts and L-cuts on the timeline.

### Fixed

- Cropping a clip no longer adds zoom keyframes or starts it zooming. The crop box, the Crop numbers and the nudge keys change the zoom only while Start, End or a keyframe is picked in the Zoom section. Otherwise they only crop, and a clip that already zooms keeps its motion, the whole zoom moving with the crop.
- After S near where one shot's sound runs on under the next, or starts early under the one before, Join puts the two pieces back. It used to refuse, and joining with Alt left the picture and its sound apart, so dragging the picture left the sound behind.
- Dragging a shot's head edge longer on V1, where the next shot's sound leads in from before it, no longer cuts that sound in two and runs this shot's sound over it. The next shot moves on whole, its sound with it.
- Pressing I on a sound inside its lead-in, before its picture starts, now closes up on every track. Before, a title on V2 over a later shot stayed where it was and ended up over a different frame.

The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ZazaGdev/editbay/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

**SHA-256 of `Editbay.Setup.1.2.exe`:**
`f31644ba5d49789c72652222ac92a07c53d818e39f7f8d170a87f3c6e1c115f2`

The installer is not code signed. Check the hash with `certutil -hashfile "Editbay.Setup.1.2.exe" SHA256`.

name: Editbay 1.1
body:
Editbay 1.1: a security fix for projects someone else sends you, and smaller fixes to the timeline. Update if you open projects from other people.

### Added

- `Ctrl+A` selects every clip on the timeline, on every track. It can be changed in the shortcuts window, and in a text field it still selects the text.

### Fixed

- **Security:** a project someone sent you could make Windows sign in to their computer, and so hand over your password hash, through the preview: its player read a playlist dressed as an `.mp4` and followed it to a network share. Every file the window loads is now checked, and one on a share you have not allowed is refused; a source that is really a playlist opens as missing.
- Taking out, or trimming with O or a ripple drag, the shot before one whose sound starts early (a J-cut) no longer leaves black frames on V1 or moves a title over the shot before.
- Ctrl+wheel over the timeline keeps zooming about the pointer. While a clip played it jumped back to the playhead after a notch or two.
- The band drawn at a clip's edge on the timeline is narrower, 16 pixels at a cut. The area that grabs a trim keeps its size.

The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ZazaGdev/editbay/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
